item.title: U.S. measles cases more than double what they were last year as outbreak spreads
item.description:

U.S. measles cases more than double what they were last year as outbreak spreads
October 25, 20264:35 PM ET
By
Chandelis Duster
A sign is posted outside a Pennsylvania Department of Health measles vaccination clinic located in Lancaster County in Peach Bottom, Pa., Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026.
Matt Rourke/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Matt Rourke/AP
The U.S. is grappling with its worst resurgence of measles in decades, with cases particularly high in the state of Pennsylvania.
New data from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention shows there have been more than 4,580 measles cases across the U.S. since Oct. 22, which is more than double the number for the whole of 2025.
The vaccination status of 96% of those who contracted measles in 2026 was "Unvaccinated or Unknown," according to data from the CDC.

A measles outbreak across Pennsylvania has grown as officials urge residents to get fully vaccinated against the disease.

U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche Sunday defended his department's lawsuit seeking to stop Alaska from automatically certifying the results of its Senate election if the Republican incumbent there loses.
Earlier this week he had said the Justice Department could get involved in the vote certification process in a "doomsday" scenario.

item.title: Venezuela's opposition leader María Corina Machado returns after months in exile
item.description:
World
Venezuela's opposition leader María Corina Machado returns after months in exile
Updated October 25, 20267:31 PM ET
Originally published October 25, 202612:18 PM ET
Carrie Kahn
Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, center, greets supporters in Barquisimeto, Venezuela, on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026.
Jesus Hernandez/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Jesus Hernandez/AP
Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado has returned to Venezuela after ten months abroad, announcing her arrival in a social media post.
In a post on X, Machado declared: "I'm here, with you all."
Machado made her first public appearance among worshippers at the Church of Santa Rosa in Lara state, western Venezuela, where she was quickly surrounded by an ecstatic congregation. She then travelled on to Caracas, where hundreds of cheering supporters swarmed her car. "Here" she tweeted, when she arrived in the capital.
Her return poses a challenge to interim President Delcy Rodríguez, who took over after U.S. forces captured former leader Nicolás Maduro in January.

item.title: This College of Magic turns ordinary kids into cool magicians
item.description:
This College of Magic turns ordinary kids into cool magicians
October 25, 20267:24 AM ET
By
Julie Bourdin
,
Photos by Tommy Trenchard
Lubelo Mthenjana, who's 11, performs a magic trick involving fire during the annual junior magic contest at the College of Magic in Cape Town, South Africa.
Tommy Trenchard for NPR
hide caption
toggle caption i
Tommy Trenchard for NPR
Dressed in a sharp black three-piece suit and a dapper yellow bow tie, Lubelo Mthenjana stands alone on a dark stage, taking in the last few seconds of quiet before the curtain opens. He takes a deep breath as his name is announced. Then he opens his arms wide and flashes a bright smile.
"Hello everyone! My name is Lubelo Mthenjana, and I will be performing for you … some magic!"
The audience of about 30 children and parents is spellbound. They laugh out loud as he makes a string of paper clips vanish into a plastic cup and gasp with surprise as the clips reappear inside a matchbox. Then comes his best trick: He conjures sweets out of thin air and tosses them into the crowd. The room erupts. As Lubelo takes his final bow to thunderous applause, his mom beams a proud smile at the 11-year-old apprentice magician.
